title: Circular Economy Energy Transitions and Sustainable 2 Growth in BRICS Economies: Distributional Heterogeneity 3 and the Energy Rebound Effect
content: This study examines the distributional heterogeneity of circular economy (CE) energy transitions and their relationship with economic growth across six BRICS economies—Brazil, China, India, South Africa, Egypt, and Indonesia—from 2000 to 2025. Using the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) as the primary estimator, with fixed effects as a robustness check, we assess effects across the growth distribution while accounting for cross-sectional dependence and panel integration properties. We also provide a direct estimate of the energy rebound effect for the BRICS panel. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity that mean-based estimators obscure. Renewable energy share and energy intensity are positive and statistically significant mainly at middle-to-high growth quantiles (Q50–Q90). In contrast, gross capital formation and FDI are robust positive drivers across all quantiles. Urbanization is negatively associated with growth at Q25–Q90, while trade openness and domestic credit are largely insignificant in the MMQR specification. The rebound-effect estimate indicates that approximately 25.7% of energy efficiency gains are offset by increased consumption, implying net savings of about 74.3%. These findings suggest that CE energy transitions do not affect all economies uniformly: investment and foreign capital remain broad-based growth engines, whereas energy transition dividends are concentrated in faster-growing economies. The study offers differentiated policy implications for low-, middle-, and high-growth BRICS economies and cautions against one-size-fits-all CE prescriptions.
